name: France
governanceModel: EU AI Act member state pursuing sovereignty through infrastructure, not new law
debateTopics: Mistral's defense-AI partnership and dual military/commercial strategy
Silicon sovereignty — AMD/SiPearl vs. NVIDIA dependence
SecNumCloud sovereignty vs. US hyperscaler participation
overview:
France governs AI through the EU AI Act as a member state, but its real national AI strategy is industrial: an approximately €109 billion national AI infrastructure package announced at the February 2025 AI Action Summit, anchored by Mistral AI's rapid rise into a genuine frontier lab. Mistral now runs 'Mistral Compute' — 18,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Superchips in a 40MW data centre — and has been selected by the Ministry of the Armed Forces under a three-year defense-AI framework deal.

France is also pursuing 'silicon sovereignty' distinct from NVIDIA dependence, extending the Jean Zay supercomputer with AMD and European SiPearl chips, and enforcing data-sovereignty through ANSSI's SecNumCloud certification for sensitive workloads.

currentDirection.summary: France's AI Act obligations are unchanged as an EU member state; the real momentum is industrial policy — a roughly €109B infrastructure package, Mistral's compute build-out, and a push toward European silicon to reduce NVIDIA dependence.

recentDevelopments.text: Mistral opens early access to a new open-weight mixture-of-experts model; EU AI Act enforcement powers (information requests, model access, recall) activate 2 August 2026; a further €4B French/Swedish data-centre build-out is announced.
Mistral AI selected by the Ministry of the Armed Forces under a three-year defense-AI framework deal.
Mistral Compute launches with 18,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Superchips in a 40MW Essonne data centre.
Jean Zay supercomputer extended with AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and SiPearl European CPUs, an explicit 'silicon sovereignty' move distinct from NVIDIA dependence.
SoftBank reportedly plans up to 5GW of French AI data-centre capacity, with an initial €45B phase covering 3.1GW by 2031.
Mistral AI closes a €1.7B Series C at an €11.7B valuation, with ASML as lead investor taking an 11% stake.

policyAndRegulation.title: National AI infrastructure package
policyAndRegulation.summary: Roughly €109B package announced at the February 2025 AI Action Summit combining sovereign, private and EU funding for data centres, GPU capacity, and research grants via Inria and Université PSL.

policyAndRegulation.title: SecNumCloud certification
policyAndRegulation.summary: ANSSI-run sovereignty certification requiring physical hosting on French soil; doesn't exclude US hyperscalers if they comply, but signals a distinct national data-sovereignty posture.

policyAndRegulation.title: AI Act (as applied in France)
policyAndRegulation.summary: France's AI governance runs through the EU AI Act as a member state, with no distinct comprehensive national AI statute of its own.

researchEcosystem.summary: Inria coordinates France's national AI research strategy through the PEPR AI programme (CNRS, CEA and Inria, €73M over six years) and nine university AI clusters (€360M under France 2030), building on the original 2018 AI for Humanity strategy.

debates.topic: Mistral's defense-AI partnership and dual military/commercial strategy
debates.summary: Mistral's three-year framework deal with the Ministry of the Armed Forces raises questions about how a commercial frontier lab balances defense work with its consumer and enterprise business.
debates.expanded: As Mistral becomes both France's commercial AI champion and a defense contractor, questions arise about data separation between military and civilian use cases, and whether defense revenue changes the incentives of a lab that also positions itself as Europe's open, sovereign alternative to US and Chinese labs.

debates.topic: Silicon sovereignty — AMD/SiPearl vs. NVIDIA dependence
debates.summary: France is deliberately diversifying away from NVIDIA for some national compute infrastructure, pairing AMD GPUs with European SiPearl CPUs.
debates.expanded: The Jean Zay supercomputer's extension with AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and SiPearl European CPUs is a direct, practical hedge against NVIDIA's near-monopoly on AI training hardware — though Mistral's own Mistral Compute infrastructure still runs on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell chips, showing the sovereignty push is partial rather than total.

debates.topic: SecNumCloud sovereignty vs. US hyperscaler participation
debates.summary: France's cloud sovereignty framework requires French-soil hosting but doesn't exclude US hyperscalers outright, a middle path between full sovereignty and full dependence.
debates.expanded: SecNumCloud certification lets AWS, Microsoft and Google potentially qualify if they meet French hosting and operational requirements, which critics say dilutes the sovereignty goal, while supporters argue it's the only realistic way to get sovereignty-grade infrastructure at hyperscale speed.
